title: Palisades (Holtec restart): External_Sender To NRC: Palisades: Opposed to Restart/Tipped Fuel Rod Assembly/Plans [['E-Mail']]

documents.text:
From:             Kary Love
To:               Marlayna Doell
Subject:          [External_Sender] To NRC: Palisades: Opposed to Restart/Tipped Fuel Rod Assembly/Plans
Date:             Thursday, October 8, 2026 8:53:34 AM


Dear Ms. Doell: I reside and work within the "evacuation zone" of Palisades Nuclear Plant. I oppose
Holtec's proposed fuel rod assembly loading plan.

Holtec International officials said that on Aug. 30 workers were loading fuel assemblies into the reactor
when one tilted and the fuel-handling grapple machine disengaged.

As you are aware this is only the most recent "problem" encountered in this "experiment" in nuclear plant
resurrection:


              The fuel assembly incident is the most recent delay in Holtec’s effort to restart
              Palisades, which could become the first U.S. nuclear plant to return to
              generating electricity after entering the decommissioning process.

              Earlier delays in the restart were caused by extensive repairs to steam
              generators required after inspectors found defects in the equipment.


An NRC inspection report issued Aug. 31 cited Holtec for other low-level violations involving work done
between December 2025 and March 2026. Inspectors found that Palisades failed to properly control
radioactive contamination and evaluate potential internal radiation doses to workers.

The demonstrated history above supports the conclusion “systemic quality assurance shortfalls” at
Palisades exist under Holtec's unprecedented attempts to "restart" the aged plant that has exceeded by
many years its engineered "safety lifetime."

The NRC has documented this danger and potential damage should the "restart" continue its checkered
run:


                     A 1982 NRC report (CRAC-II, short for Calculation of Reactor
                     Accident Consequences, also known as the 1982 Sandia Siting
                     Study or NUREG/CR-2239) estimated Palisades' meltdown
                     would cause: a thousand acute radiation poisoning deaths;
                     7,000 radiation injuries; 10,000 latent cancer deaths; and more
                     than $50 billion in property damage downwind and downstream.
                     Adjusting for inflation alone, property damage would now
                     surmount $175 billion in current dollar figures. And the
                     Associated Press has warned that, given population growth
                     near American atomic reactors like Palisades over the past
                     several decades, a proportional increase in casualty figures
                     would also result, given more people live, work, and recreate in
                     harm's way. AP also cited neutron-embrittlement of the reactor
                     pressure vessel (RPV), and risk of through-wall fracture from
                     pressurized thermal shock, as a top example of NRC
                     weakening safety regulations to accommodate continued
                     operations at age-degraded reactors. NRC has admitted that
                     Palisades, and the Point Beach Unit 2 reactor, also on Lake
                     Michigan's shore in Wisconsin, are the two worst-embrittled
                     RPVs in the country. Watchdogs have warned about Palisades'
                     embrittlement for more than three decades.
 Given the potential downsides to Holtec's failures to date and probable future failures given the
complexity of issues facing the "restart" and the fact a nuclear plant has never been successfully
resurrected, the NRC ought terminate the attempt and require closure and clean up. Thank you.



Kary Love
17344 Wood Drift Drive
West Olive, MI 49460
